title: Applying Financial Stress Testing Methodology to AI Model Portfolios

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: stress testing directly addresses correlated failure. A regulatory-grade tool would be immediately useful for organizations assessing their AI portfolio resilience.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The stress testing concept is well-documented (DFAST/CCAR frameworks). Scenario design uses existing safety benchmark methodology. Intermediate difficulty: accessible with guidance for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: define a small set of adverse scenarios, run a portfolio of models through them, measure correlated vs. independent failure. Clear experiment design achievable in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: While AI-driven stress testing of financial portfolios is actively studied, the reverse direction — applying financial stress testing methodology (DFAST/CCAR-style adverse scenarios) to AI model portfolios to measure correlated safety failures — is a distinct and largely unaddressed idea. The ESRB (2025) and FSB (2024) discuss AI systemic risk but from a financial regulation perspective, not as a methodology to stress-test AI deployments. A GNN approach to stress testing (EMNLP AgentScen 2025) applies to financial scenarios, not AI model portfolios. The specific contribution of defining adverse scenarios and measuring correlated vs. independent failure in a portfolio of AI models is novel as an empirical methodology.
